To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HPV is involved in the development of esophageal squam-ous cell carcinomas.
HPV DNA sequences can be detected in 43.1 percent of esophageal squamocellular carcinomas and in 49.0 percent of the adjacent precancerous lesions.

the HPV involvement in human esophageal carcinogenesis was demonstrated by a series of systematic analyses of a total of 71 esophageal squamouus cell carcinomas, using light microscopy, electron microscope (TEM), in-situ hybridization (ISH), Southern blot hybridization (SBH), and the polymerase chain reaction technique (PCR).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of the presence of human Papilloma virus (HPV) infection in the esophageal cancer tissue by using different DNA techniques.
the role of HPV in the pathogenesis and progression of esophageal precancers and squamous cell carcinoma.
the detection of HPV in esophageal cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HPV infection is not the sole cause of esophageal squinous cell carcinoma.
HPV infection may be a causative factor in esophageal carcinogenesis, but further studies are needed to elucidate the role of HPV in esophageal cancer.
HPV infection is not a necessary cause of esophageal squamocellular carcinoma, but that the infection may play an etiologic role in a significant proportion of esophageal cancers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HPV is involved in esophageal cancer.

HPV infection may contribute to esophageal carcinogenesis by inducing the formation of precancerous lesions, which may then progress to frank carcinomas through the action of additional carcinogenic agents.
HPV infection is involved in a significant proportion of esophageal carcinogenesis and that HPV 18 seems to be more frequently involved than HPV 16.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HPV DNA can be detected in esophageal cancer and its precursors.
HPV infection is a common finding in esophageal carcinomas and may play a role in esophageal tumorigenesis.
HPV is a major cause of esophageal cancers and that the HPV vaccine is an important tool in prevention.
